zh.q: 这台仪器叫什么？手柄、塔轮、长槽、横臂、套筒、标尺各干什么？为什么读出来的是「格数」而不是「牛顿」？
zh.concl: 小球做匀速圆周运动，向心力由横臂挡板对球的压力提供；球对挡板的反作用经杠杆使套筒下降、露出标尺。教材 p.29 原话是「根据标尺上露出的红白相间等分标记，可以粗略计算出两个球所受向心力的比值」——这台仪器给的是比值，不是两个力各多少牛。
points: 八个部位各有分工：手柄给转速、塔轮给角速度比、长槽给半径、横臂挡板给压力、套筒与标尺把压力变成格数；名牌里的数字（手柄 1、长槽 4、短槽 5、变速塔轮 2·3）是教材图6.2-4 的部位编号，不是刻度或档位。
读的是比值不是牛顿：教材自己写「粗略计算出两个球所受向心力的比值」，标尺只能数整格。
向心力不是第四种力：这里是「挡板对球的压力」，别在图上再加一条向外的「离心力」。

zh.q: 为什么要先把两球调成「同质量、同半径、同角速度」？这时两个标尺应该露得一样多，露得不一样说明什么？
zh.concl: 教材 p.29 的实验是两球同时转、同时读，所以任何一个量不一样，读出来的就不是那一个量的影响；四项都对上以后标尺等高（格数比 1.00），这台仪器才算「调好了」——这也是后面三步能成立的前提。
points: 演示器是两球同时转、同时读的仪器：任何一个量不同，标尺差就不是「那个量」的功劳。
「仪器自检」= 四项对齐（同质量、同半径、同角速度、同转速），判据是两标尺等高（格数比 1.00）。
手柄要匀速转（教材 p.28 原句），转速抖的时候套筒会自己上下动。

zh.q: 只换球、别的都不动：露出的格数会翻倍吗？为什么不能同时把球挪远一点？
zh.concl: 只改质量时，格数比等于质量比 ⟹ F ∝ m。教材 p.29 那句提问「怎样才能在改变某个物理量时保持其他物理量不变」，这里就是答案：球的质量换了，半径档和皮带档一个都不许动。
points: 判定「只改了一个量」：半径档、皮带档、转速档一个都不许动。
三组要落在过原点的直线上（斜率 1.000），不是「看起来一样」。
质量翻倍、格数翻倍 ⟹ F ∝ m（一次方）。

zh.q: 把长槽的球挪到 6.0 cm、8.0 cm，格数会变几倍？是跟半径成正比，还是跟半径的平方成正比？
zh.concl: 只改半径时，格数比等于半径比 ⟹ F ∝ r（一次方，不是平方）；半径翻倍、力也翻倍，而线速度也翻了倍（v = ωr）——所以「F ∝ v²」与「F ∝ r」并不矛盾：v 变大时 r 也变大。
points: 半径是一次方：8.0 cm 比 4.0 cm 远一倍，格数也只多一倍。
同一时刻线速度也变了（v = ωr），所以「F 与 v 的平方成正比」和「F 与 r 成正比」不是两件事。
长槽上三档刻线要对准球心，球的位置就是半径。

zh.q: 皮带从同层挪到差一层、差两层，右球转得快了 2 倍、3 倍——格数会变 2 倍、3 倍吗？
zh.concl: 右球角速度变 2 倍，向心力变 4 倍；变 3 倍，变 9 倍 ⟹ F ∝ ω²（不是 ω 的一次方）。教材 p.26 练习第 3 题说的「摩擦传动不打滑 → ω 跟 r 成反比」就是这一步塔轮比 1:2:3 的来路。
points: 塔轮换层改变的是两侧的角速度比（1 : 2 : 3）；手柄转速对两侧同时变、不产生比值差。
格数比随 ω 的平方变：2 倍 → 4 倍，3 倍 → 9 倍。
8/72 = 0.11 就是 1/9；三档读数都是精确的，取整误差只在真实档出现（第 7 步）。

zh.q: 三个量合起来该怎么写？三个量同时都不一样，格数比还可能等于 1.00 吗？
zh.concl: 三个量合起来就是 Fn = mω²r；用它和 v = ωr 一步换出 Fn = m v²/r（教材 p.29 同一页的两个红框公式）。两个不同工况能拼出同一个格数比，只有「三个量的幂次分别是 1、1、2」才做得到——这是本课最硬的一条证据。
points: 三个量合起来：Fn = mω²r，再用 v = ωr 换成 Fn = m v²/r（同一页两个红框，是同一条规律）。
「不同工况拼出同一个格数比」是幂次为 1、1、2 的直接证据。
会算教材 p.30 第 3 题：0.10 kg、0.10 m、4 rad/s → 0.16 N（教材没印答案，是按 p.29 的式子代进去算的）。

zh.q: 皮带脱开时右标尺为什么一格都不露？「真实器材」档打开后格数比为什么变成 0.29 而不是 0.25？
zh.concl: 皮带打滑使右球转得比标称慢 → 右向心力偏小 → 格数比偏大（方向写死在 A2.18，能复算）；格数比那几个百分点不是规律不成立，而是教材自己说的「粗略」：标尺只能数整格（两侧各 ±0.5 格，比值误差上界 0.5/左 + 0.5/右）。
points: 皮带打滑的方向能算：(1/0.94)²−1 = +13.2 %，格数比偏大。
标尺只能数整格 → 格数比误差上界 0.5/左格数 + 0.5/右格数（8/8 时 12.5 %）。
转速太高会超量程（右球 288 格 > 80 格），读数作废而不是「偏大」。

zh.q: 两球质量相同、半径相同，只动皮带档——用标尺记 3 组，能不能当场判出格数比跟 (角速度比)² 成正比？
zh.concl: 没有新结论：把第 5 步的方法用一遍——只改一个量 + 两标尺格数比 + 过原点直线。考 ω 的平方而不是 r 的一次方，是因为学生最容易在这里错（以为快 2 倍就多 2 倍格数）。
points: 考核只动皮带档，质量与半径（4.0 cm）一律不动。
3 组数据要能画出对 (ω比)² 的过原点直线，斜率 ≈ 1。
皮带 III 那一组读 8 / 72 = 0.11，也就是 1/9 —— 快 3 倍、格数差 9 倍。

en.q: What is this instrument called? What do the crank, stepped pulleys, long slot, lever arm, sleeve and scale each do? Why does it read "divisions" rather than "newtons"?
en.concl: Each ball moves in uniform circular motion, with the centripetal force supplied by the push of the lever stop on the ball; the ball's reaction on the stop works through the lever to lower the sleeve and reveal the scale. Textbook p.29: "from the red-and-white equal divisions exposed on the scales, the ratio of the centripetal forces on the two balls can be roughly calculated". This instrument gives a ratio, not how many newtons each force is.
points: Each of the eight parts has a job: the crank sets the speed, the stepped pulleys the angular velocity ratio, the long slot the radius, the lever stop the force, and the sleeve and scale turn force into divisions. The numbers on the labels (crank 1, long slot 4, short slot 5, stepped pulleys 2·3) are the part numbers in textbook Fig. 6.2-4, not scale marks or settings.
It reads a ratio, not newtons: the textbook itself says "roughly calculate the ratio of the centripetal forces on the two balls", and the scale can only count whole divisions.
Centripetal force isn't a fourth kind of force: here it's "the push of the stop on the ball", so don't add an outward "centrifugal force" to the diagram.

en.q: Why first set both balls to "same mass, same radius, same angular velocity"? The two scales should then show the same amount; what does it mean if they don't?
en.concl: In the experiment on textbook p.29 both balls turn and are read at the same time, so if any one quantity differs, the reading isn't the effect of that one quantity alone; only when all four match and the scales are level (ratio 1.00) is the instrument "set up". This is the premise for the next three steps.
points: The demonstrator spins and reads both balls at once: if any quantity differs, the scale difference isn't due to "that one quantity".
"Self-check" = all four matched (same mass, radius, angular velocity, speed), and the test is level scales (ratio 1.00).
Turn the crank steadily (textbook p.28 wording); if the speed wobbles, the sleeves bob up and down by themselves.

en.q: Change only the balls, nothing else: do the divisions double? Why can't you move a ball outward at the same time?
en.concl: Changing only mass, the division ratio equals the mass ratio ⟹ F ∝ m. The textbook's question on p.29, "how can you keep other quantities fixed while changing one?", is answered here: the balls change, and neither the radius setting nor the belt setting may move.
points: Check that "only one quantity changed": don't touch the radius, belt or speed settings.
The three sets must lie on a line through the origin (slope 1.000), not just "look the same".
Double the mass, double the divisions ⟹ F ∝ m (first power).

en.q: Move the long-slot ball to 6.0 cm and 8.0 cm. By what factor do the divisions change? Is it proportional to radius, or to radius squared?
en.concl: Changing only radius, the division ratio equals the radius ratio ⟹ F ∝ r (first power, not squared); double the radius and the force doubles, but the linear speed also doubles (v = ωr), so "F ∝ v²" and "F ∝ r" don't conflict: as v grows, so does r.
points: Radius is first power: 8.0 cm is twice as far as 4.0 cm, and the divisions only double.
The linear speed changes at the same time (v = ωr), so "F proportional to v squared" and "F proportional to r" aren't two separate things.
The three marks on the long slot line up with the ball's center; the ball's position is the radius.

en.q: Move the belt from the same step to one step apart, then two: the right ball turns 2 and 3 times as fast. Do the divisions change 2 and 3 times?
en.concl: Double the right ball's angular velocity and the centripetal force quadruples; triple it and the force is nine times ⟹ F ∝ ω² (not ω to the first power). Exercise 3 on textbook p.26, "friction drive without slipping → ω is inversely proportional to r", is where the 1:2:3 pulley ratio in this step comes from.
points: Changing pulley steps changes the angular velocity ratio between the two sides (1 : 2 : 3); the crank speed changes both sides together and creates no ratio difference.
The division ratio changes with ω squared: 2 times → 4 times, 3 times → 9 times.
8/72 = 0.11 is 1/9; all three readings are exact, and rounding error only appears in real mode (step 7).

en.q: How do you write the three together? With all three quantities different at once, can the division ratio still be 1.00?
en.concl: Put the three together and you get Fn = mω²r; with v = ωr it becomes Fn = m v²/r in one step (the two boxed formulas on textbook p.29). Two different setups can only give the same division ratio if the three quantities' powers are 1, 1 and 2: this is the lesson's strongest evidence.
points: Together the three give Fn = mω²r, which v = ωr turns into Fn = m v²/r (two boxed formulas on the same page, the same law).
"Different setups giving the same division ratio" is direct evidence that the powers are 1, 1 and 2.
Work out textbook p.30, question 3: 0.10 kg, 0.10 m, 4 rad/s → 0.16 N (the textbook doesn't print the answer; it's calculated from the formula on p.29).

en.q: With the belt off, why does the right scale show no divisions at all? With "Real equipment" on, why is the ratio 0.29 instead of 0.25?
en.concl: Belt slip makes the right ball turn slower than nominal → right-side centripetal force too small → ratio too large (the direction is fixed in A2.18 and can be recalculated); the few percent off in the ratio don't mean the law fails; it's the "roughly" the textbook mentions: the scale can only count whole divisions (±0.5 division each side, ratio error bound 0.5/left + 0.5/right).
points: The direction of belt slip can be calculated: (1/0.94)²−1 = +13.2 %, ratio too large.
The scale counts whole divisions only → ratio error bound 0.5/left divisions + 0.5/right divisions (12.5 % at 8/8).
Too high a speed goes over range (right ball 288 divisions > 80), and the reading is void, not "too high".

en.q: Two balls of equal mass at equal radius, changing only the belt: can you record 3 sets on the scales and show on the spot that the division ratio is proportional to (angular velocity ratio)²?
en.concl: No new conclusion: use step 5's method once more, changing one quantity + division ratio of the two scales + line through the origin. It tests ω squared rather than r to the first power because that's where students most often go wrong (thinking twice as fast means twice the divisions).
points: The assessment only changes the belt setting; mass and radius (4.0 cm) stay fixed.
The 3 sets must give a line through the origin against (ω ratio)², with slope ≈ 1.
The belt III set reads 8 / 72 = 0.11, i.e. 1/9: three times as fast, nine times the divisions.
